newsitem.title: RWANDA: US Congressman suggests stop feeding Rwanda refugees.
newsitem.headline: US Congressman suggests stop feeding Rwanda refugees.

text.p: A U.S. congressman said on Tuesday stopping feeding Rwandan refugees was one way to make them go home and suggested a U.N. force to escort them across the border.

Congressman Harry Johnston, a member of the African affairs sub-committee, and congressman Douglas Peterson said the problem of an estimated 1.1 million Rwandan refugees in Zaire was destabilising the region and hopes for democracy in Rwanda.
"The international community and Rwanda should work together to close these camps and encourage refugees to return," Johnston told a news conference in the Rwandan capital Kigali.

"Stopping feeding in the camps is an alternative, but it may take pressure to bring in a U.N. security force to escort refugees across the border and guarantee security to returning refugees," he added.
"This security force is not just hypothetical. When you look at the operations in Cambodia that were successful you will see it is a real possibility," he added.
The two congressmen were speaking after talks in Rwanda with government officials and parliamentarians and in Kenya with exiled Rwandan opposition leaders.
"We need to address the problems of the Zairean and Tanzanian armies being able to impose discipline in the camps, and to prevent human rights violations," Johnston said.
"As long as the camps in eastern Zaire are bases for terrorism, the problem will continue."
There are about 600,000 Rwandan refugees in Tanzania who, like those in Zaire, fled Rwanda during the genocide of up to an estimated one million people and three months of civil war in 1994.
Many refugees say they fear reprisals if they go home. Aid workers say Hutu former Rwandan troops and militiamen who took part in the genocide are intimidating them against returning.
Rwandan Hutus inflitrating from refugee camps are waging a guerrilla war with Rwandan government troops in border areas.
